chunks: My father (may father (may he be blessed) with this chain narrated, saying: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:
One who has a house and a believer needs to live in it, but he prevents him from it,
Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: 'O My angels! This man is acting miserly in giving shelter to My servant in this world. And by My honor, he will never live in My Gardens (Paradise) forever.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual consequence of denying a believer housing when you have the means?
ai.summary: In *Thawab al-A'mal*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq’s (a) declaration that withholding housing from a needy believer constitutes a specific form of miserliness (*bukhl*) against Allah’s own servant. This hadith emphasizes the reciprocal nature of divine hospitality: just as the owner denied temporary worldly shelter, Allah denies them eternal residence in His gardens (*Jinan*), a concept rooted in the Shia understanding of *Adab* (etiquette) towards fellow believers as extensions of the Divine presence.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: one who has a house and if a believer desires to live in that house but the former does not allow him,
the Almighty Allah says, “O My angels! This man is acting miserly in giving shelter to My servant in this  world. I swear  by My  honor, he  will never receive  a place in My Paradise.”
